doc.title: Harry Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Working backwards from Scott Hamilton to the older tenors
summary: Through Hamilton he became aware of Webster, Young, Hawkins, Gonsalves, Sims and Getz.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Maybe you didn’t go to class that year. Did your tastes in music work backwards. After working in your head with Scott, did you go back farther than that?

Not really my taste so much as my awareness of where Scott came from and through listening to Scott I began to be aware of Ben Webster and Lester Young and Coleman Hawkins and Paul Gonsalves and Zoot now and Stan Getz. And so I went backwards in that sense — not so much a taste sense but just an awareness.
